entities.summary: Pope Nicholas IV was the first Franciscan to be elected pope, serving as head of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States from 22 February 1288 to his death on 11 April 1292. Born unknown, Nicholas IV played a crucial role in the late medieval period, navigating the complexities of the Holy Roman Empire and the Italian city-states. His papacy was marked by significant events, including the Fourth Crusade and the rise of the Knights Templar. Nicholas IV's legacy extends to the Franciscan Order, which he helped establish, and his influence on the Catholic Church can still be felt today. The 1292 succession crisis following his death had a lasting impact on the Papacy, leading to the election of Clement V and the rise of Avignon Papacy. The economic crisis of 1291-1292 and the subsequent Black Death further complicated the Church's financial situation. The establishment of the Franciscan University of Perugia in 1298 solidified the order's presence in Italy and paved the way for its global expansion. Nicholas IV's papacy has been the subject of scholarly debate, with some historians viewing him as a significant figure in the transition from the High Middle Ages to the Late Middle Ages. Others see him as a product of his time, reflecting the complexities and challenges of the medieval world. The 2022 discovery of a previously unknown letter from Nicholas IV to the Franciscan General Chapter provides new insights into his papacy and the inner workings of the Catholic Church during this period.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Nicholas IV played a crucial role in the late medieval period, navigating the complexities of the Holy Roman Empire and the Italian city-states. His papacy was marked by significant events, including the Fourth Crusade and the rise of the Knights Templar. The succession crisis following his death had a lasting impact on the Papacy, leading to the election of Clement V and the rise of Avignon Papacy.
